events.title: Roman conquest of the Helvetii
hints: A tribe's planned migration was halted at Bibracte in 58 BCE.
A conquest of the Alps completed the subjugation by 15 BCE.
events.summary: Julius Caesar defeated the migrating Helvetii at the Battle of Bibracte in 58 BCE and forced them back to their homeland. The Alpine region was fully subdued in 15 BCE and became part of the Roman provinces.

events.title: French invasion and the Helvetic Republic
hints: Troops marched into a city in March 1798 and seized the state treasury.
A sister republic with a new constitution was imposed until Napoleon's mediation in 1803.
events.summary: French troops invaded in 1798 and took the Bernese treasury, then created the centralised Helvetic Republic as a client state. French occupation and requisitioning continued until Napoleon's Act of Mediation of 1803.

events.title: Foreign armies fighting in the Alps
hints: A Russian field marshal marched an army across the Alps in the autumn of 1799.
The battles of Zurich saw three great powers fight on the country's soil.
events.summary: In 1799 French, Austrian and Russian armies fought across the country during the War of the Second Coalition, culminating in the Second Battle of Zurich and Suvorov's crossing of the Alps. The conflict devastated much of central Switzerland.
